tools.name: record_work
tools.description: Record a build-work summary into FoxPlug as a milestone (source: Claude Code). Call this at the end of a session. It captures what you shipped so FoxPlug can score it and surface the shippable moments in your Radar. It never posts anything. Free — capture is not metered. Do NOT include secrets, keys

tools.name: log_update
tools.description: Tell FoxPlug what you just finished building, in one short plain paragraph. Call it after a change a user would notice (user_facing true) or after plumbing nobody outside needs to hear about (user_facing false, which is kept out of drafts and counts toward "not worth a post"). It never posts anythin

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: This week's brief from FoxPlug: one thing to fix, one to say and one to skip, with where each number came from. Ask it when the founder wonders what to post. Read-only. It does not rebuild the brief; the founder presses Build the brief in FoxPlug.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description: The latest post drafts FoxPlug wrote for the founder (channel, status, text). Read-only; nothing is posted or changed.

tools.name: simulate_buyers
tools.description: Before you merge or ship, ask your buyers. Give the change as the buyer would see it (pricing text, a feature description, launch copy). tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Set the current plan, intent, or priorities for a project in FoxPlug (source: Claude Code). Call this when you set or change what a project is working toward, so FoxPlug knows the goal your later work is measured against. It replaces the project's previous current plan. Free — it never posts anythin

tools.name: check_drift
tools.description: Check whether a project's recent work still matches its current plan. FoxPlug compares the plan you set (via set_plan) against the work recorded since, and returns an alignment verdict with any divergences — work that is off-plan, or plan items nothing has moved toward. Read-only judgment; it never

tools.name: get_plan_status
tools.description: Get where a project stands: its current plan, how much work has been recorded since the plan was set, and the latest drift verdict (if any). Read-only and cheap — it runs no judgment, so use it to pull current state without re-running check_drift. It never posts anything. Free.

tools.name: what_nobody_knows
tools.description: What this project shipped that nobody outside it knows about. Counts the milestones worth talking about in a window and how many of them were actually posted, and names the loudest silent ones. Read-only — it generates nothing and posts nothing. Free.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: What FoxPlug remembers about this maker, with an epistemic status on every fact: settled (more than one observation, none contradicting), thin (seen once), contested (the evidence disagrees with itself), superseded (replaced by something later — never propose it again). Read-only. Free.

tools.name: supersede_fact
tools.description: Mark a remembered fact as finished, so it is never proposed again. Takes the fact id from recall and a REASON — a fact struck out without a reason cannot be restored. This is the only one of these tools that changes anything, and it changes memory, never anything public. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_brief, list_drafts, check_drift, get_plan_status, what_nobody_knows · Private data: record_work, log_update, set_plan · Public sink: log_update, get_brief, list_drafts.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_brief, list_drafts, check_drift, get_plan_status, what_nobody_knows · Private data: record_work, log_update, set_plan · Public sink: log_update, get_brief, list_drafts

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
